subject: Clarion Health DPA: operational proof for no-training & data custody
messages:
From: Maggie Higgins <maggie.higgins@clarionhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Clarion Legal <legal@clarionhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarion DPA redlines — no-training proof and transfer paths

Jonas —

Thanks for the redline (attached). Legal had two blocker asks we need operational confirmation on before we can proceed:

1) A firm, contractual no-training commitment (no model improvement) for customer inputs + a description of the technical and process controls you will use to enforce this.
2) Evidence that we can reasonably expect for compliance reviews: subprocessor inventory, cross-border transfer path for backups/replicas, and an attestation confirming onshore key control (KMS) for US-hosted data.

Two additional smaller asks:
- Can Clarion be assigned clear ownership of prompts and generated responses (so we have output IP assurances)?
- Timeline: Clarion is trying to close this week; can you provide the evidence package and an ETA on the attestation?

Attachments: Clarion-DPA-Redline-v3.pdf (our proposed edits)

Appreciate a short, itemized reply we can circulate to Legal.

— Maggie
Director of Partner Privacy
Clarion Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Maggie Higgins <maggie.higgins@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarion DPA redlines — no-training proof and transfer paths

Maggie —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, then a proposed evidence checklist and ETA below.

1) No-training commitment: we will accept and sign an explicit no-model-improvement clause that prohibits use of Clarion customer inputs for training or model updates. Operationally we implement this via:
   - a contractual toggle scoped per-tenant that disables any downstream training pipelines for those inputs;
   - request routing to a non-adaptive serving fleet that has learning/adaptation paths removed;
   - KV/prefix caching set to ephemeral-only (TTL <= 60s) and excluded from any persistent corpora;
   - strict telemetry filters so sampling/telemetry exports exclude opted-out tenant IDs.

2) Evidence & transfer paths: we can provide the following deliverables:
   - Subprocessor inventory export (CSV) with roles and regions;
   - Dataflow diagram showing primary and replica storage, backup retention windows, and cross-border hops (PNG/PDF);
   - Onshore KMS attestation (we use customer-scoped KMS keys in the US on Dedicated/Private plans; for Hosted we provide HSM-backed envelope keys and can show key usage logs);
   - SOC 2 excerpt relevant to change control and access logging.

Ownership of prompts/responses: we will accept an output-IP assignment clause for customer-generated prompts and model outputs in the DPA. Practically we also offer:
   - exportable transaction logs and delivery of prompt/response bundles on request (SFTP or secure Drive link);
   - option to disable telemetry retention entirely for Clarion accounts.

ETA & next steps:
   - Kimberly and Neha will own the evidence pack. We can deliver a first bundle (subprocessors CSV + dataflow PNG + attestation draft) by Thu 17 May EOD PT.
   - SOC2 excerpt and full subprocessor spreadsheet with contact fields by Mon 20 May.
   - We'll redline your DPA to include the specific no-training paragraph and an output-IP clause and return for DocuSign review by Tue 21 May if the evidence looks OK.

Attachments we will provide: redwood-attestation-no-train.txt, dataflow-diagram.png, subprocessor-inventory-202805.xlsx, SOC2-excerpt.pdf

If Clarion legal has preferred language, send the snippet and we'll mirror it in our amendment. Happy to do a 20-minute call if you prefer.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Maggie Higgins <maggie.higgins@clarionhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Clarion Legal <legal@clarionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarion DPA redlines — no-training proof and transfer paths

Jonas / team —

Appreciate the clear commitments. A few follow-ups from Legal:

- Subprocessor detail: we need not just names and regions but the exact processing purpose and whether subcontractors have access to non-anonymized prompts/responses. Any chance you can mark processors that handle backups/replicas separately?
- Backups & cross-border: what is the lifecycle of backups (retention, deletion process) and do backups ever transit outside the US for replication or DR testing?
- Evidence format: Legal wants a signed attestation (paper or DocuSign) we can keep on file rather than a self-service CSV.

Also: Clarion requires a contractual clause that grants them the right to request a one-time export of all prompts/responses and a snapshot of associated metadata (timestamps, tenant id, request id) for a 30‑day period, deliverable within 10 business days. Is that feasible operationally?

Timeline: the team is reviewing the planned deliverables you listed. If you can get the attestation + highlighted subprocessor rows by EOD today (17 May) that materially helps move this forward.

Thanks —
Maggie

Clarion asks: one-time export of prompts/responses + metadata — operational note: we can produce an export for a 30-day window and deliver via secure SFTP within 10 business days. Next steps / timeline:

  - Tue 21 May: we will send a DPA amendment with the explicit no-training paragraph + output-IP clause for signature
  - Upon signing: we commit to the 10-business-day export SLA and will schedule the export delivery.

Best,
